tx_frontside_boulders_2.blurb: Frontside Boulders is part of the Parking Lot Boulders at Bull Creek Park, a creekside pocket of bouldering inside Austin's northwest suburbs. The problems sit a short stroll from the car under tree cover, which keeps things comfortable well into warm weather. Most of the climbing is on the easier side, with plenty of V0 to V3 and a smaller group of harder lines that reach into the V6 to V8 range. It suits a quick session, a mixed-ability group, or a warm-up before heading to the nearby harder boulders. Bring a pad or two and keep valuables out of the vehicle.
tx_frontside_boulders_2.parking_note: Reach the park from Loop 360 via Lakewood Springs Drive, cross the creek, and use the unpaved lot beyond it. The boulders lie a short walk to the north. Leave nothing visible in the car.

tx_seismic_wall_a_k_a_maggie_s_wall.blurb: Seismic Wall, also called Maggie's Wall, is a bolted sport wall on the Barton Creek Greenbelt in south Austin. It faces south, so it takes plenty of sun, though the wooded setting still throws some shade; mornings and late afternoons suit hot weather, and cooler days favor the afternoon. The routes run from around 5.6 into the 5.12 range, with the bulk between 5.9 and 5.11, and a handful of top-rope and trad lines mixed in. It is a short walk in, and the rock dries quickly after rain. Some older hardware is questionable, so a helmet and a careful look at the bolts are sensible.
tx_seismic_wall_a_k_a_maggie_s_wall.approach: A brief downhill trail leads from the lot to Barton Creek, with the wall visible on the far side. The creek crossing can be slick after rain.

tx_kingdom_of_ging.blurb: Kingdom of Ging is a small, quiet wall at the Gus Fruh end of the Barton Creek Greenbelt, best known for bouldering with a handful of sport routes beside it. The limestone is solid, and a long shallow cave runs along the base. Trees shade the wall for most of the day and traffic is light. The problems span from the moderate V2 range up to a few very hard lines, with the greater share in the V6 to V8 band; the sport lines start around 5.10 and go into the low 5.13s. Expect a creek crossing on the way in, and bring several pads since landings are tall.
tx_kingdom_of_ging.approach: From the Gus Fruh entrance, ford the small creek and take the marked trail to the right. The big in-cut cave along the base shows you where the climbing starts.

_expect.name: Dairy Farm / Frog Pond Boulders, The

tx_dairy_farm_frog_pond_boulders_the.blurb: The Dairy Farm and Frog Pond boulders sit on the south side of the Main Dome at Enchanted Rock, in the pink granite that makes the whole park famous. They are among the easiest boulders in the park to reach, which makes them a natural first stop for a bouldering day. The problems lean friendly, with most between VB and V2, and a smaller number of harder lines pushing up toward V8. The granite is coarse and abrasive, so expect tired skin, and more boulders are scattered nearby for anyone who wants to wander.
tx_dairy_farm_frog_pond_boulders_the.parking_note: Use the main day-use lot inside the park; the boulders are reached on foot from there.
tx_dairy_farm_frog_pond_boulders_the.approach: Follow the trail from the main lot past the gazebo and around the south flank of the dome. It is a short walk of roughly five to ten minutes.

tx_main_wall_2.blurb: The Main Wall is the busiest bouldering section at Tonkawa Falls, a small creekside city park outside Crawford, west of Waco. The rock is pocketed limestone beside a little waterfall, and the problems are lined up close together along the wall. Most are on the gentle end, with plenty of V0 to V3, while a few stand out much harder, reaching into the V10 range. It tends to be uncrowded and low key. Summer heat is the main drawback, so cooler months are more pleasant, and a crash pad is worth carrying down.
tx_main_wall_2.parking_note: Enter Crawford's city park through the large gate east of downtown and leave the car in the gravel area near the falls.
tx_main_wall_2.approach: A short trail and a set of stairs lead down from the pavilion to the base of the wall.

tx_big_rocks_park.blurb: Big Rocks Park is a riverside city park in Glen Rose where low limestone boulders sit along the Paluxy River just upstream of a small dam. It is a modest, local-flavored spot rather than a destination, with problems mostly in the easy to moderate range, from V0 to about V4. The boulders get plenty of sun, so cooler months or evenings feel better. After heavy rain the river can cover some of them, and swimmers fill the area on summer weekends. Bring a pad for the uneven landings.
tx_big_rocks_park.parking_note: The nearest lot is by the Methodist camp off Highway 144. Another option is to leave the car at Heritage Park downtown and follow the riverside concrete path about half a mile.
